old.claim: For any $n\geq1$ and $Z\in M_n(\mathbb C)$, use the standard inner product $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_k u_k\overline{v_k}$, linear in its first argument, and define $|u\rangle\langle v|$ as the map $x\mapsto\langle x,v\rangle u$. Since $Z^*Z$ is positive, with $\langle Z^*Zv,v\rangle=\|Zv\|^2$, [F3] diagonalizes it in an orthonormal basis $(v_j)$ with eigenvalues $s_j^2\geq0$. For each $s_j>0$, put $u_j=Zv_j/s_j$. Then $\langle u_j,u_k\rangle=\delta_{jk}$, and $Z=\sum_{s_j>0}s_j|u_j\rangle\langle v_j|$. The positive square root of $Z^*Z$ has eigenvalues $s_j$, so $\|Z\|_1=\sum_j s_j$.
